verdict.rationale: Auth0 documents the OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Flow as a first-party capability: a device app passes its Client ID to start authorization and get a token, while the user approves on a separate computer or phone. Auth0's own MCP Server uses this flow to let AI tools like Claude Desktop authenticate, which shows the flow in use for agent tooling rather than pasted secrets. Missing for 10: docs frame the flow around input-constrained devices such as smart TVs rather than CLIs or headless agents explicitly, there is no evidence the Auth0 CLI itself logs in this way, and there is no independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can authenticate CLIs and headless agents via the OAuth device authorization flow instead of pasting long-lived secrets

citations.quote: device apps use the Device Authorization Flow (ratified in OAuth 2.0), in which they pass along their Client ID to initiate the authorization process and get a token.
the device asks the user to go to a link on their computer or smartphone and authorize the device.
Use the Auth0 MCP Server to manage your Auth0 tenant through natural language with AI tools, like Claude Desktop, using secure OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization.
